xBRIEFInfo.description: Scope xBRIEF ingested from GitHub issue #6648

plan.title: enhancement(xbrief): PROJECT-DEFINITION has grown past 1 MiB with no bound or pruning path

narratives.Description: xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json is about 1.09 MB because plan.items holds one row for every scope, and most rows are finished scopes that already have their own brief files. This story keeps plan.items to open scopes only (proposed, pending, active), keeps the row set current on lifecycle moves, bounds the narrative staleness flags to one line per narrative, and re-renders the file once so it drops under 1 MiB.
narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer, I want the project definition to list open scopes only, so that its size stays flat as stories complete and no reader hits a buffer limit by surprise.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. Add one open-folder constant beside PROJECT_LIFECYCLE_FOLDERS and project plan.items from it; keep scanning completed/ only for staleness flags. 2. In the PROJECT-DEFINITION sync path, match rows by source_path or filename stem, remove on a move into completed/ or cancelled/, and patch or insert on a move into an open folder, using the row builder render uses; leave the specification registry sync unchanged. 3. Make flagStaleNarratives emit one line per narrative. 4. Update docs/FILES.md. 5. Run project:render once and commit the smaller file. Not built here: clauses 7, 17 and 18 (the doctor size line); they stay in the brief and get a disposition at completion because doctor output belongs to the installer lifecycle owner (docs/installer-refactor-ovpr/LLM-CONTEXT.md section 5).
narratives.Overview:
1. Open-only projection. `renderProjectDefinition` builds `plan.items` from the `proposed`, `pending` and `active` folders only, named by one constant next to `PROJECT_LIFECYCLE_FOLDERS`. Completed and cancelled briefs are not copied into the file. Render still scans `completed/` to compute staleness flags (item 4); it does not store those rows.
2. Project-definition sync on a move into `completed/` or `cancelled/` (complete, fail, cancel). The PROJECT-DEFINITION sync removes every row whose `metadata.source_path` resolves to the old or new brief path, or whose `id` equals the brief's filename stem (the row id render writes; not the dateless remainder that `scopeIdsForFilename` also returns). It never matches by title.
3. Project-definition sync on a move into `proposed/`, `pending/` or `active/` (restore, promote, activate, and any other move whose target folder is open). When a row matches by the rule in item 2, it is patched as today (status, `source_path`, `lifecycle_folder`). When no row matches, one row is inserted, built by the same row builder that render uses. It matches as in item 2 and never by title.
4. Bounded staleness flags. `flagStaleNarratives` emits at most one line per narrative: the narrative name, the count of matching unacknowledged completed scopes and the shared words. Today's summary line stays. The flag list stays an array of strings. The acknowledgement id list and `parseStalenessReview` are unchanged.
5. Specification untouched. `syncRegistryArtifactAfterScopeMove` keeps its current behaviour (patch, with today's matcher) for the specification registry. Items 2 and 3 apply only on the PROJECT-DEFINITION sync path.
6. First shrink. The implementing PR runs `project:render` once and commits the smaller file. No migration verb.
7. Size visible. `doctor` prints one information line: the PROJECT-DEFINITION size in bytes, the 64 MiB reader capture limit (`SUBPROCESS_MAX_BUFFER`) and the 1 MiB target. Above 1 MiB the line says the file is over the target and that `project:render` drops completed and cancelled registry rows. The line is printed through the info output, on the full probe and on the throttled return alike, and never changes the doctor exit code or warning count.
8. Docs. The xBRIEF layout docs state that `plan.items` lists open scopes only, that finished briefs live in their folders, the 1 MiB target and the 64 MiB limit, and that the greenfield export's implementation plan therefore lists open scopes only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given briefs in all five lifecycle folders, when `project:render` runs, then `plan.items` holds exactly the briefs in `proposed/`, `pending/` and `active/`.
- Given an active scope with a PD row, when `scope:complete` moves it to `completed/`, then its row is removed and no other row is changed.
- Given two PD rows with the same title and different files, when one of those scopes is completed or cancelled, then only the row for the moved file is removed.
- Given a scope with no PD row in `cancelled/`, when `restore` moves it to `proposed/`, then PD has one row for it, equal to the row render would build.
- Given a PD row for a proposed scope, when it is promoted to `pending/`, then that row is patched with the new status, `source_path` and `lifecycle_folder`, and no row is added.
- Given a lifecycle move, then `specification.xbrief.json` changes exactly as it does today.
- Given 50 unacknowledged completed scopes whose titles share words with one narrative, when render runs, then `staleness_flags` holds at most one line for that narrative.
- Given an existing `staleness_review` id list, when render runs, then scopes in that list are not flagged.
- Given a PROJECT-DEFINITION over 1 MiB, when `doctor` runs, then it prints the size line naming the target, the 64 MiB limit and `project:render`, and its exit code and warning count are the same as without the line.
- Given a doctor run that takes the throttled return, then the size line is still printed.
- Given a PD row whose id is the dateless remainder of a moved brief's filename and that has a different `source_path`, when that brief is completed, then that row is not removed.
- After the first-shrink render on this repo, `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` is under 1 MiB and `validateProjectDefinition` reports no new errors.
narratives.Constraint:
- Removing rows with today's shared matcher, including title match, or applying removal to the specification registry (comment 6970404830, finding 1).
- A timestamp watermark for staleness acknowledgement, or a hash of the id list (comment 6970404830, finding 2).
- An archive file or a split index for finished rows: the brief files in `completed/` and `cancelled/` already are that record, and no reader needs a second copy.
- A size gate or refusal at any threshold (issue, Expected).
- Documenting 1 MiB as the supported maximum (comment 6970404830, finding 4).
